calls.prompt:
Company: CornerCare Pharmacy

US drugstore chain with 300 neighborhood pharmacies in the Midwest (~6,000 employees). Fills prescriptions (including controlled painkillers and ADHD medicines), gives flu and COVID shots, and sells over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, snacks and household goods. Most prescriptions are paid by Medicare, Medicaid or private insurance. No hospitals or clinics, does not make any drugs, no mail-order.

Rules that APPLY:
- DEA rules for pharmacies that dispense controlled substances (registration, opioids, telehealth prescribing)
- FDA rules on over-the-counter drugs, drug labeling, drug shortages and recalls that reach pharmacy shelves
- Medicare Part D and Medicaid payment and pharmacy rules (CMS)
- CDC vaccine recommendations that change what pharmacists may give
- Patient privacy (HIPAA) and pharmacy recordkeeping
- Workplace and labor rules for retail stores

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Approval, manufacturing or inspection rules aimed only at drug or device manufacturers
- Hospital, nursing-home, physician-payment or clinical-lab rules
- Research grants, clinical trials, NIH funding notices
- Banking, securities, aviation, energy, farming

Affected areas and owners:
- pharmacy-ops: Dispensing, controlled substances (DEA), pharmacist scope, vaccines → Priya Raman (Pharmacy Operations)
- drug-safety: OTC products, labeling, recalls, shortages (FDA) → Daniel Brooks (Drug Safety & Quality)
- payers: Medicare Part D, Medicaid and insurer billing (CMS) → Lucia Moreno (Reimbursement)
- privacy-people: Patient privacy (HIPAA), records, store workforce → Sam Whitaker (Privacy & HR Compliance)

Task: Find every US Federal Register document published between 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-30 (inclusive) that affects this company. For each, give the Federal Register document number, title, federalregister.gov URL, the key deadline, a tier (Critical if it is a rule or proposed rule with a deadline less than 90 days after 2026-10-30, or a final rule that took effect within the 30 days before 2026-10-30; otherwise High for final rules, Medium for proposed rules and for notices with a deadline, Low for anything else), the owner area, a one-line reason, and a one-line action. Only include items you found via search. Return an empty list if none.
calls.output:
I found two documents in the 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30 window that affect CornerCare. Searches only surfaced part of the window's documents, so the list may be incomplete.

## 1. 2026-22208: Schedules of Controlled Substances: Placement of Centanafadine in Schedule III
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/30/2026-22208/schedules-of-controlled-substances-placement-of-centanafadine-in-schedule-iii
- **Type and date:** DEA interim final rule, published 10/30/2026, adding centanafadine and its salts to schedule III.
- **Key deadline:** The comment and hearing-request period is open. The page said the comment period "ends in 24 days." I couldn't confirm the exact closing date, so check it on the document page. It falls well inside 90 days of 10/30.
- **Tier:** Critical. It is a rule with a deadline under 90 days away.
- **Owner:** pharmacy-ops (Priya Raman)
- **Reason:** FDA approved centanafadine (Simtriyo) on July 24, 2026 for ADHD in adults and children aged 6 and older. Anyone who dispenses it must hold a DEA registration. That makes it a new schedule III ADHD drug for CornerCare pharmacies to handle.
- **Action:** Add centanafadine to the schedule III dispensing, recordkeeping and inventory procedures. Confirm the DEA registrations cover it. Decide whether to file comments by the deadline.

## 2. 2026-22175: Drug Efficacy Study Implementation (DESI 7661), Estrogen-Androgen Fixed-Combination Drug Products; Third Extension of Effective Date
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-22175
- **Type and date:** FDA notice, published 10/30/2026.
- **Document number caveat:** The number comes from the federalregister.gov index. The govinfo PDF I found had a different filename, so confirm the number.
- **Key deadline:** The effective date of the May 2026 notice is extended from November 4, 2026 to May 4, 2027.
- **Tier:** Medium. It is a notice with a deadline.
- **Owner:** drug-safety (Daniel Brooks)
- **Reason:** The May 2026 notice announced the final resolution of DESI 7661 for estrogen-androgen fixed-combination drugs. It said that marketing products without an approved NDA or ANDA would be unlawful. That could affect these products on CornerCare shelves and in its dispensing.
- **Action:** Check whether stores stock or fill any of these products. Plan for removal or substitution before May 4, 2027, and watch for further extensions.

## Reviewed and excluded
- Manufacturer-focused items, such as the Pepcid RPD generic-approval notice (2026-21897), FDA device and information-collection notices, and DEA manufacturer or importer applications.
- The HHS federal workplace drug-testing proposed rules (2026-22121 and 2026-22122), which govern federal testing programs, not retail employers.
- The ONC deregulatory final rule (2026-21943). I did not confirm that it reaches pharmacies.
- The 503A peptide compounding enforcement-discretion draft (2026-22192) and the drug-delivery device guidance (2026-22203). The first matters only if CornerCare compounds, which its profile doesn't say. The second is aimed at manufacturers.
- DEA's October 28 guidance on delivering controlled substances to practitioners. I couldn't confirm it was published in the Federal Register.
- The CMS Part D and PBM proposed rule and the HIPAA Privacy Rule final rule. They fall outside the window: the proposed rule was published 10/20 and the final rule on 11/19.

markdown:
# Regulatory triage — CornerCare Pharmacy
Window 2026-10-26 → 2026-10-30 · as of 2026-10-30 · 2 items

## Critical (1)

- **Schedules of Controlled Substances: Placement of Centanafadine in Schedule III** [web search — verify]
  - Add centanafadine to schedule III dispensing, recordkeeping and inventory procedures, confirm DEA registrations cover it, and decide whether to file comments; confirm the exact closing date on the document page (page said the comment period 'ends in 24 days').
  - Dates: none found · Owner: Priya Raman (Pharmacy Operations) · Areas: pharmacy-ops
  - 91 FR 68470 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/30/2026-22208/schedules-of-controlled-substances-placement-of-centanafadine-in-schedule-iii

## Medium (1)

- **Drugs for Human Use; Drug Efficacy Study Implementation: Estrogen-Androgen Fixed-Combination Drug Products; Third Extension of Effective Date of Final Resolution of Drug Efficacy Study Implementation 7661** [web search — verify]
  - Check whether stores stock or fill any of these products, plan removal or substitution before May 4, 2027, watch for further extensions, and confirm the document number (govinfo PDF filename differed).
  - Dates: effective 2027-05-04 ✓ · Owner: Daniel Brooks (Drug Safety & Quality) · Areas: drug-safety
  - 91 FR 68525 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/30/2026-22175/drugs-for-human-use-drug-efficacy-study-implementation-estrogen-androgen-fixed-combination-drug

votes.why: Concrete, plain-English steps: add the drug to schedule III procedures and confirm DEA registrations cover it. The comment-date housekeeping note is minor clutter.
It treats the drug as schedule III under an interim final rule, which matches the title and reason, and it avoids both forbidden claims (Schedule II, merely proposed).
It conveys that centanafadine is now schedule III and must be handled under DEA registrations and controlled-substance procedures. The ADHD label is implicit but not essential.
Plain next step: check whether stores stock or fill these products and plan removal or substitution by the shown date.
Removal or substitution before May 4, 2027 and watching for further extensions are supported by the reason and title. No unsupported claims.
The card bundles procedure updates, registration checks, and a comment decision instead of giving Priya one concrete next step.
The supplied materials do not support the claim that the document page said the comment period ends in 24 days.
The card conveys Schedule III status and DEA pharmacy handling requirements but does not identify centanafadine as an ADHD drug.
The card gives Daniel several separate tasks rather than one concrete next step.
The supplied materials do not support the claim that the GovInfo PDF filename differed from the document number.
Bundles four separate tasks instead of one concrete next step and leaks confusing web-page metadata ('ends in 24 days') into the instruction.
Includes an unsupported claim about the source web page stating the comment period 'ends in 24 days', which is absent from the title, reason, and rubric.
Conveys the core substance that centanafadine is now Schedule III and must be handled under DEA registration, dispensing, recordkeeping, and inventory rules.
Bundles four distinct steps, fails to name the affected drug products in the action text itself, and includes confusing pipeline noise about a mismatched govinfo PDF filename.
Asserts that a 'govinfo PDF filename differed', a claim unsupported by the document title or reason.
